key_insight: Domain-wall energy from B2 ordering affects coercivity only weakly; the large hardening in printed Fe–49Co–2V is dominated by retained defects, not antiphase-domain size.
engineering_relevance: For additive manufacturing of soft magnets, process control should prioritize reducing in-build defects rather than relying on post-build annealing to eliminate excess coercivity.
method: Compared additively manufactured and wrought Fe–49Co–2V at matched grain size.
Calibrated wrought material with a known order parameter to fix the ordered-state domain-wall energy.
Tested the effect of ordering and antiphase-domain size on coercivity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that ordering falls orders of magnitude short of the measured coercivity excess, and a tenfold change in antiphase-domain size leaves coercivity unchanged.
watch_item: The conclusion depends on the specific alloy, calibration state, and matched-grain-size comparison, so transfer to other compositions or processing routes should be validated.
paper_title: Domain-wall energy governs coercivity in ordered and disordered additively manufactured Fe--49Co--2V
